summary: noxleys@1.1.1: WhatsApp/Baileys-family library with unverified static patterns
details: noxleys@1.1.1 is a WhatsApp/Baileys-family messaging library. Static keyword co-occurrence patterns fired in lib/Utils/messages-media.js and lib/Utils/chat-utils.js: require("child_process"), require("os"), require("http")/require("https"), fetch() and POST calls, Buffer.from() decoding, and process.version references. The only network host observed in the cited evidence is https://mmg.whatsapp.net, which is WhatsApp's own media endpoint used by the Baileys family for legitimate media upload/download. The pattern shape (child_process + http + os + Buffer.from base64) is also the ordinary shape of a media-handling library that spawns ffmpeg/sharp-like helpers and decodes/encodes media payloads. No specific installer secret read, no non-first-party exfiltration destination, and no install/import-time fetch-and-execute path is present in the cited evidence. package.json lifecycle hooks were not implicated by the findings. As a fork/derivative of Baileys, noxleys inherits the covert-side-effect risks previously observed in that family (e.g., auto-subscribe using the installer's session), which cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the available evidence alone.
